question: Positive control: given the actual nearby colored exterior of a matched vacant center, is its single archived arrangement more predictable than from cold training prevalence alone? This is a different question from prediction by the distant R=4 shell. Its result cannot rescue that experiment or demonstrate independent-cavity recurrence, formation dynamics, equilibration, or point-to-set order.
target: Vacant center; exactly three occupied and three vacant axial arms. Match the sorted coordination numbers of the occupied arms. A tripod has one vacancy per axis; a T has an opposite vacant pair. Scan every one of 8000 periodic native z,y,x origins exactly once per parent; retain every match with unit weight. No choice of frame, orientation, preferred arm, cap or parent filter. No new configurations, replicas, trajectories or sampling.
data_firewall: Sole primary is index 7 FULL native validation. Descriptive only: index 9 FIRST 1024 validation parents in native split order (slice BEFORE extracting microscopic bytes; never read center arrays on the 1024 reserved issue parents), then full index 0 validation. No input from test, index 6, or other cohorts. Compressed-file authentication and ZIP decompression may stream through skipped byte ranges. Each parent/lineage appears once within a cohort. No cross-temperature pairing.
prevalence: Use the archived cold-lock signature and pairing-lock.train_counts_T_tripod = [77991,48533], from the full native index 9 TRAIN census. Baseline is the raw center prevalence 48533 / 126524, NOT the earlier smoothed fit/tune intercept, shell forecast, a 0.5 shape prior, or an intercept recomputed on any evaluated data.
inputs: Only the 56 actual exterior species at integer offsets of Manhattan distance 2 or 3 in z,y,x order are passed to the finite law, with known beta and locked signature. Center/arm labels, interior species/composition, parent, coordinates, fitted coefficients, and observed frequencies are not inputs. Eligibility and observation are computed separately. Condition on the matched event, not its occurrence probability.
law: Enumerate all 20 sets of three occupied arms (8 tripod, 12 T). For an admissible mask the occupied arms see the same multiset of nearest-neighbor counts. Summing central species decorations at fixed counts factors out of the relative weights; even knowing only the mixture of counts is unnecessary for the ratio. For each occupied distance-2 exterior site j let d_j be its coordination with the whole cross empty minus its species preference. With s_j adjacent occupied arms the exterior energy increment is 2*d_j*s_j+s_j^2. Exact weights are exp(-beta*sum of these increments). Linear drops only shared-neighbor pair penalties, retaining all single-arm fields. Feasible weights are equal per admissible MASK, not per admissible shape. At beta=0 all three laws coincide. This is the exact conditional law for the specified canonical Hamiltonian, not a claim that released endpoints are exact equilibrium draws.
decision: Pass only if the lower endpoint of the two-sided 95% interval for paired EXACT minus frozen cold prevalence observed log-score gain is >= 0.01 nat per matched center across ALL matches at index 7. Unidentified interval never passes. No fitted parameters, replacement cohorts, temperature pooling, retries or alternate success conditions.
uncertainty: For per-parent numerator sums d_i and matched-center counts w_i use G=sum(d_i)/sum(w_i). Pair within parent BEFORE inference. All P native parents stay in, including zero-count parents. SE=sqrt(P/(P-1) sum_i(d_i-G*w_i)^2)/sum(w_i), two-sided t_(P-1,0.975). Zero total count gives a null estimate; fewer than two contributing parents gives no interval. The same unit and estimator apply to subset, calibration, and reliability diagnostics.
support_and_numerics: Determine structural 0/1 only from zero feasible-mask count for one shape; the observed shape must ALWAYS be feasible. In a forced cage require exact, linear and feasible to predict the unique shape with probability 1, scoring 0 log loss exactly. In an ambivalent cage both shapes have positive theoretical mass. For computing logs only, replace a returned float64 endpoint 0 or 1 there with eps/2 or 1-eps/2, respectively. Keep all interior floats unchanged; use log1p(-p) for T. Report endpoint-repair counts. Never clip away an impossible observed event or call a rounded extreme structurally forced.
diagnostics: For all matches AND ambivalent matches (at least one admissible mask of each shape), separately report prevalence, forecasts, actual log scores, accuracy (p>=1/2 calls tripod), expected log score and expected accuracy under the exact conditional law, and paired model contrasts vs prevalence, vs equal feasible masks, vs linear fields. Identify geometrically forced fraction and each forced shape count. Report observed minus predicted calibration and observed minus oracle-expected scores/accuracy, with whole-parent intervals; reliability bins fixed as [0,.1),...,[.9,1] with model mean, observed frequency and exact-oracle probability. These are descriptive, not ground truth from independent cavities or an additional pass test.
artifacts: An exclusive near-run.json claims the one score before any endpoint access. near-parents-II.npz retains parent rows, chain identity, match/shape counts and sufficient sums by subset, forecast, and reliability bin; near-score-II.json links each NPZ. near-results.json binds score JSON, NPZ and figure hashes and primary decision. near-cage.png shows primary/secondary gains and the ambivalent energetic comparisons. No score output may be replaced.
